result.question: Finance wants a number for Transformer 1 at site MAIN. If the gas trend means we'll need corrective oil work soon, how many hours and how much will it cost? Check whether hydrogen, ethylene and acetylene rose between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, give their daily rates in ppm/day, and project each forward 7 days from the last sample. If any projection crosses its IEEE C57.104 Condition 1 limit, treat corrective work as likely within the week. The limits are 100 ppm for hydrogen, 50 ppm for ethylene and 1 ppm for acetylene. Then look through the closed work order history on Transformer 1 for similar corrective jobs, such as oil treatment, degassing, filtration or internal inspection. Give me their average actual hours, average actual cost and average overrun versus plan, and use those to estimate the likely job. If corrective work is likely and no open work order already covers it, draft a work order carrying that estimate in the notes, and give me the MAIN site's overall backlog and overdue counts so I can see what it competes with. If no similar closed work orders exist, say so. In that case, base the estimate on the average of all closed Transformer 1 work orders and label it low-confidence. If none of the gases is projected to cross a limit, don't create a work order. Just report the estimate as a contingency figure.
result.answer:
I can't give Finance a number for this job. Transformer 1 has no closed work orders, so there are no past hours or costs to base an estimate on. Corrective oil work does look likely within the week. I tried to create the work order, but the work-order system rejected it with "403 Forbidden", so no work order exists yet.

**Gas trend, 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-18** (the last sample in the window is 2024-01-18)

| Gas | First → last | Daily rate | Did it rise? | Level on 2024-01-25 (7 days on) | Condition 1 limit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hydrogen | 2,845 → 2,900 ppm | +18.33 ppm/day | Yes | ~3,028 ppm | 100 ppm |
| Ethylene | 16,684 → 16,600 ppm | −28.0 ppm/day | No, it fell | ~16,404 ppm | 50 ppm |
| Acetylene | 7 → 7 ppm | 0 ppm/day | No, flat | 7 ppm | 1 ppm |

The rates are straight-line from first to last sample. All three gases are already far above their limits, and all three stay above them over the next 7 days. So corrective work counts as likely within the week, even though only hydrogen is rising.

**Estimate**
- **Similar closed jobs:** none. Transformer 1 has no closed oil treatment, degassing, filtration or internal inspection work orders.
- **Fallback:** none either. Its only two work orders are still open, so there's no closed history to take a low-confidence average from.
- **Average actual hours, cost and overrun versus plan:** can't be calculated. The job needs an estimate from a vendor quote or a standard job plan.

**Open work orders on Transformer 1**
Neither covers oil treatment or degassing, so a new work order is warranted:
- **1000052:** retest the oil gas sample and check insulation (corrective, priority 3, waiting for approval).
- **1000051:** inspect the on-load tap changer (predictive, priority 1, waiting for approval).

**Draft work order: not created**
I drafted a corrective work order for oil treatment (degassing and filtration) plus internal inspection, at priority 2. Its notes held the gas trend and projections and stated that no estimate is available. Whoever manages the work-order service needs to grant write access before it can be created.

**What it would compete with at MAIN**
- **All time:** 4 open work orders, of which 2 are overdue. Those are 1000045 (Chiller 6, due 2020-04-30) and 1000046 (Pump 3, due 2020-05-03).
- **Last 3 months:** 2 open work orders (the two Transformer 1 ones above), none overdue.
